chunks: And he also narrated it from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Zakariyya ibn Imran, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Nothing comes into being in the heavens nor in the earth except by seven — by (divine) ordainment, determination, intention, desire, writing, term, and permission. So whoever claims other than this has lied against God or rejected (the word of) God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أَجَل: Appointed term/time; the divinely fixed moment at which something concludes
key_terms.إِذْن: Divine permission; the authorizing leave without which nothing can occur
key_terms.إِرَادَة: Divine intention/will; God's deliberate purpose in bringing something about
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a formulaic honorific for God
key_terms.قَدَر: Divine determination; the measure and proportion God assigns to created things
key_terms.قَضَاء: Divine ordainment; God's executive decree that something shall occur
key_terms.كِتَاب: Divine writing; scriptural recording of decrees in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)
key_terms.مَشِيئَة: Divine desire/wish; distinct from irada, referring to God's volitional choice

ai.seo_question: What are the seven aspects of divine decree according to Imam Musa al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) enumerates seven divine prerequisites for every event in creation: qada (divine decree), qadar (divine measure), irada (intention), mashi'a (desire), kitab (scriptural decree), ajal (appointed term), and idhn (permission). This hadith is a foundational Shia theological statement on divine determinism, establishing that nothing in existence occurs except through the complete and purposeful agency of God. Any denial of these seven aspects constitutes either fabricating a falsehood against God or rejecting His word outright.
